lines.text: Privaty slides the door open.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Everyone...!
As soon as she does...
we see the curtains that had once decorated the walls so beautifully now tattered into ribbons,
with a lot of half-eaten food left on the desks.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: What happened here?

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: A customer came in,

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: and before we could take her to her table, she started going crazy!

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: She tore the classroom apart.

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: While everyone went into the hall so we could clean up, all the food ingredients disappeared too.

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: The dishes we prepared are completely ruined.
Everyone looks devastated.

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: I knew it...

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: We're not meant to be doing these sorts of events.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: To be honest, there's a part of me that's kinda relieved...

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: It's a weird feeling.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: Well, since there's nothing for us to sell,

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: does anyone wanna go get parfaits?
They're talking as though they're sick of the festival,
or as though none of this was ever important to them...
They're ready to go back to their normal, everyday lives.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: We're gonna head out.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: Don't worry about cleaning up. We'll do it tomorrow.
The group all seems excited as they pack their things.
They're happy to be leaving this classroom.
Watching them, I...
Say nothing.
Stop them.
There's nothing I can do.
No more words that I can say.
The way they looked as they were preparing for this festival is a far cry from the laughter we hear outside the classroom.
Somewhere along the way, things went horribly wrong.
But when...?
I recall something Rei said...

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: This isn't very fun though.

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: I had more fun greeting customers casually with a "Hey, Master!"

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: Now, it's just...

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: starting to feel like homework.

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: It makes me not want to do it.

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: I'm not saying I won't do it.

lines.speaker: rei
lines.text: I'm just telling you how I feel.
Right...
She told us, but we didn't listen.
Privaty's eyes look as though she's about to break down. She must be thinking the same thing as me.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: ... Mr. {AccountData.NickName}.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I think we might've gone about this the wrong way.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: To me, a festival should be fun.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I was hoping it would really take root here and become a part of the school's culture.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I didn't want it to be canceled forever just because of some random evaluation that we don't even know the criteria for.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: But...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: what's the point of continuing to hold a festival that isn't fun for students in the moment?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: That doesn't sound like a very "perfect" festival...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: There was nothing perfect about the looks on their faces...!
Calm Privaty down.
Share the blame.
I pull her into a hug,
and slowly pat her back.
Calm down. We can still turn this around.
The students did their best. We just need to do the same.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Do you really think we can do that...?
We're the teachers.
Of course we can.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: ... I wasn't going to say this because I didn't want it to go to your head,

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: but I'm really glad that you're here with me.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: If I were alone, I think I would've collapsed under the guilt.
I doubt that. You would've found a way, even if you were alone.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: ... Maybe.
Privaty and I clean up the wrecked classroom.
We put away the decorations and rearrange it in a low-key, cozy way using things we were able to buy for cheap.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: *Yaaawn*

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: What time is it now?
... Three forty in the morning.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: *Sigh...*

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: We're almost done, but I'm exhausted.
I figured you would be...
so I brought a couple beers!
I pull out two cans from the fridge where the ingredients were stored.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Oh wow.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: That's... surprisingly thoughtful of you.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Thank you.
*Thack! Fizz...*

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Do we have anything we could eat?
Want me to try making omurice with the ingredients we bought earlier?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Haha, sure.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I'll give you a food review.
I recall the omurice we had at the maid cafe, and the one Amy made.
I do my best to recreate it.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Hmm...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Well, it's not much to look at.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: The eggs are all torn up.
She takes a bite.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Huh...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: It's really salty.
Sorry...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: No, it actually goes great with a cold beer.
I'm starting to understand how impressive Amy really is.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I know. To think she recreated that flavor in just a few days.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: She must've worked incredibly hard.
Think you can do just a little bit more today?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Yeah, let's do it!
She's right. It's all our fault.
At this point, getting a good evaluation is out of the question.
The students wouldn't want to do this again, anyway.
Yeah, we really messed this up.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: You really think so...?
I doubt there'll even be a festival next year.
All they'll remember is how bad this one was.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Oh...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Oh no...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: M-maybe if we get the students to come back now, we can...!
I doubt they'd appreciate that.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Then we can at least clean this up ourselves...!
All of this? Just the two of us?
It's okay, Privaty.
What's done is done.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I-I just...

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: I never meant to put them through that...
Let's head back.
I support Privaty as she barely has the strength to walk, and we go back to my room.
It doesn't feel right to send everyone home like this.
H-hey, everyone, wait a second!
The group stops and looks back at us.
Their eyes are empty and disengaged.
After demanding perfection this whole time, what could I possibly say to them now...?
If we all clean up together, it won't take that long...

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: *Sigh...*

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: Yeah, that's true.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: But that would mean we'd have to do this again tomorrow,

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: and we don't want that.
You all worked so hard on this, though...

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: Yeah, we really did.

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: ... But that's only because we heard it might affect our grades.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: What?!

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: What do you mean it might affect your grades?

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: There was a rumor that the festival would count toward our grades.

lines.speaker: zwei
lines.text: Was that not true?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: What?! Whoever got that idea?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: No, that's not true at all.

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: Then why did you push us so hard?

lines.speaker: amy
lines.text: Why did you make it sound like everything had to be absolutely flawless?

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Because...
Privaty and I have no answer to that.
What answer could we possibly give to a group of students who just wanted to have a fun festival?
... We're sorry.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: No, it's okay... It's not like you were trying to make things hard for us on purpose.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: We're just really tired.

lines.speaker: ein
lines.text: Can we go now?
Yeah. You did well today.
The group, who had been watching our reactions,
begin filing out of the classroom one by one.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: For today,

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: maybe it's best to just let them rest and take their minds off things.

lines.speaker: privaty_t
lines.text: Should we head back too...?
Yeah.
Privaty and I decide that we'll give them a proper apology tomorrow.
Leaving the wrecked classroom as it is, we return to the dorms.
